summary: Partial extraction with full primary-preprint reading, split named results and all 72 table rows (multiplier and center claims separated). Reuses five checked library substrates and existing global duality, class-field, Schur-cover, étale-duality and weight owners. Sources ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.3/ST.5 and InverseGalois IG.1/IG.3/IG.4/IG.5; proposes one foundational Part II for reduced Schur covers and marked central extensions. Unresolved inputs, refined-conjecture quantification, bad-type limit existence and appendix weighting are explicit gaps; no complete coverage or proof-closure claim.

items.name: Regular wreath product and quadratic projection
items.statement: For groups G and Q, G≀ᵣQ has underlying pairs (f:Q→G,a:Q) with (f,a)(h,b)=(f·(h∘L_a⁻¹),ab). Its projection to Q is a homomorphism split by a↦(1,a). For Q=C2 this is the two-factor wreath product used by Wood.
items.note: Read Mathlib/GroupTheory/RegularWreathProduct.lean:42–139. API: multiplication, projection, section, kernel and transport of the two coordinates; test the nonidentity C2 element swaps them. The coordinate identification with G×G is a consumer adapter.

items.name: Outside involutions
items.statement: For a finite group G and an embedded subgroup G′≤G≀C2, write π:G′→C2 for the restriction of the wreath projection and c={x∈G′:order(x)=2 and π(x)≠1}.
items.note: API: conjugacy stability, membership and image; test G=1 gives c={swap}. Keep the embedding as data.

items.name: Admissible wreath subgroup
items.statement: G′≤G≀C2 is admissible if it contains (1,swap), is generated by c, and ker π≤G×G projects surjectively onto the first G factor.
items.note: API: projection surjectivity, both coordinate projections, generation and transport under diagonal Aut(G). Test C3⋊inversion C2; the lone swap subgroup of C3≀C2 is not admissible.

items.name: Good subgroup
items.statement: An admissible G′ is good when c consists of one G′-conjugacy class; N_G′=#(c/G′). Thus good means N_G′=1.
items.note: API: conjugacy witness and class cardinality; tests odd cyclic G is good, diagonal G=C2 is not.

items.name: Type-preserving automorphisms
items.statement: Aut_G′(G)={α∈Aut(G):(α×α)⋊id sends the embedded subgroup G′ to itself}.
items.note: API: subgroup, action on rigid surjections and freeness; test G=1 and G=C3. This is not Aut(G′).

items.name: Global-field and infinity conventions
items.statement: Q is ℚ or Fq(t), with a chosen separable closure and a chosen place above ∞. IQ consists of imaginary quadratic K/Q: complex at ∞ for ℚ and with completion Fq(√t)∞ for Fq(t). RQ consists of quadratic K/Q split at ∞.
items.note: API: membership, transport under field isomorphism and disjointness. In the function-field case these two families do not include every possible infinity type; test the other ramified square class separately.

items.name: Maximal unramified extension split at infinity
items.statement: K^{un,∞} is the compositum in the fixed separable closure of finite extensions of K unramified at every finite place and split completely at all places above ∞; G_K^{un,∞}=Gal(K^{un,∞}/K).
items.note: API: Galois stability, profinite topology, finite quotients ↔ finite Galois extensions with these local conditions. Unit test the trivial extension. Do not omit the infinity splitting condition.

items.name: Continuous surjection moment input
items.statement: Sur(G_K^{un,∞},G) consists of continuous surjective homomorphisms to the finite discrete group G. A kernel determines an unramified G-extension split at infinity; isomorphisms of its Galois group with G give the rigidifications.
items.note: API: kernel open/normal, quotient isomorphism, postcomposition by Aut(G), and fiber cardinality |Aut(G)|. Continuity is essential.

items.name: Imaginary wreath embedding
items.statement: For K∈IQ, a rigid surjection ρ and corresponding L/K, let L̃ be its normal closure over Q and y the distinguished order-two inertia element above ∞. Embed Gal(L̃/Q) in G≀C2 by the restrictions to L and its y-conjugate, sending y to (1,swap).
items.note: API: explicit map on ker π, injectivity, compatibility with conjugation by y, surjectivity of first projection, image type. Test a cyclic cubic extension.

items.name: Imaginary extension type
items.statement: The type of an imaginary rigid surjection is the actual image G′ of the wreath embedding, rather than only an abstract isomorphism class of the normal-closure group.
items.note: API: behavior under diagonal Aut(G), equality of images, and forgetting a rigidification. Different embedded types can have isomorphic abstract groups.

items.name: Discriminant slices
items.statement: IQ_X and RQ_X restrict the respective quadratic families by absolute discriminant norm ≤X; IQ_=X and RQ_=X use equality. Over Fq(t), the norm includes the place at infinity.
items.note: API: finiteness, disjoint exact slices, monotonicity and cumulative sum. Test ramification at infinity contributes one to the discriminant degree.

items.name: Imaginary rigid finite-height average
items.statement: Ẽ⁻_≤X(G,G′) is the sum over K∈IQ_X of the number of type-G′ continuous surjections, divided by #IQ_X. Over Fq(t), Ẽ⁻_=X uses the exact-discriminant family instead. The limiting moment is the relevant X→∞ limit when it exists, with +∞ allowed.
items.note: API: numerator/denominator, nonnegative average, treatment of empty slices, finite versus infinite limit. The number-field and function-field ordering conventions must not be interchanged.

items.name: Imaginary rigid-to-unrigid conversion
items.statement: For admissible G′, the average number E⁻ of unrigid type-G′ extensions equals Ẽ⁻/|Aut_G′(G)|, at finite height and whenever the associated limit is defined.
items.note: The automorphism action on surjections with fixed embedded type is free; count its orbits.

items.name: Real twist
items.statement: For K∈RQ and a surjection ρ, a twist y is an element of order two in Gal(L̃/Q) outside Gal(L̃/K). It determines the two-factor wreath embedding sending y to (1,swap).
items.note: API: twist set, conjugation action and induced embedded type. Test that a choice is needed although inertia at infinity is trivial.

items.name: Real rigid average
items.statement: Ẽ⁺_≤X counts pairs (ρ,y) of a continuous surjection and a twist whose induced wreath image is exactly G′, averaged over RQ_X; Ẽ⁺_=X is the corresponding function-field exact slice.
items.note: API: projection to surjections, type invariance, finite-height and limit versions. Never drop y when comparing with marked Hurwitz points.

items.name: Real rigidification multiplicity
items.statement: A(G,G′) is the number of pairs consisting of an isomorphism Gal(L/K)≅G and an order-two twist whose induced wreath image is G′, for a fixed unrigid extension L/K of this type.
items.note: API: independence of representative and E⁺=Ẽ⁺/A(G,G′). The simple |c||Aut_G′(G)| formula requires goodness.

items.name: Good real multiplicity
items.statement: For good G′, A(G,G′)=|c|·|Aut_G′(G)|. Hence E⁺=Ẽ⁺/(|c||Aut_G′(G)|), with the same formula at finite height.
items.note: Proof identifies twists by conjugacy and transports the G-isomorphisms; do not use this formula for bad types without another argument.

items.name: Admissibility is necessary
items.statement: If a type occurs in the imaginary or real count over Q=ℚ or Fq(t), its embedded G′ is admissible. Consequently a nonadmissible type has zero count.
items.note: Generation uses that an everywhere-unramified extension of Q split at ∞ is trivial, after quotienting by the normal subgroup generated by inertia.

items.name: No everywhere-unramified split-infinity extension of the base
items.statement: An everywhere-unramified finite extension of ℚ, or of Fq(t) which splits at ∞, is trivial.
items.note: For ℚ use the discriminant/Minkowski result; for Fq(t) use the genus-zero unramified-cover result and exclude constant extensions by splitting at ∞. Exact supplier declarations still need matching.

items.name: Integral second group homology
items.statement: For a group F, H₂(F,ℤ) is group homology in degree two with the trivial integral representation.
items.note: Read Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/GroupHomology/LowDegree.lean:1060–1102. Reuse H2 (Rep.trivial ℤ F ℤ), cycles and quotient maps. This carrier alone does not provide Schur covers or their reduced quotient.

items.name: Schur cover
items.statement: For a finite group F, a Schur cover is a central extension 1→H₂(F,ℤ)→C→F→1 with its kernel in [C,C], equivalently with the universal-coefficient map of its extension class identifying H₂(F,ℤ) with the kernel.
items.note: The definition and existence of representation groups are already explicitly planned in upstream InductionRestriction Layer 7. Import that owner; no new ordinary Schur-cover roadmap. Do not identify this object with TauCeti.schurMultiplier, which is H²(F,kˣ). API: centrality, exactness, kernel embedding, choice and transport; test the two nonisomorphic covers of C2².

items.name: Existence and nonuniqueness of Schur covers
items.statement: Every finite group F admits a Schur cover. The cover need not be unique; D8 and Q8 give nonisomorphic Schur covers of C2². The kernel identifies with H₂(F,ℤ).
items.note: Import upstream Layer 7 existence. Reduced-cover constructions below must keep the selected cover as data.

items.name: Commutator of lifts of a commuting pair
items.statement: For commuting x,y∈F and a fixed central extension C→F, choose lifts x̂,ŷ and take [x̂,ŷ] in the central kernel. It is independent of the chosen lifts.
items.note: API: independence, conjugation invariance and functoriality under central-extension maps; test x=1 and split extensions.

items.name: Universal homological commutator
items.statement: For commuting x,y∈F, the map ℤ²→F, (m,n)↦x^m y^n sends the oriented generator of H₂(ℤ²,ℤ) to ⟨x,y⟩∈H₂(F,ℤ). Under the class map of a central extension this gives its commutator of lifts.
items.note: API: orientation/sign convention, naturality, agreement with /23. Test reversing x,y negates the class; the H₂(ℤ²) generator/comparison is a real proof obligation.

items.name: Reduced Schur multiplier
items.statement: For a conjugacy-invariant c⊆F, Q_c≤H₂(F,ℤ) is generated by ⟨x,y⟩ for x∈c and y∈C_F(x). Set H₂(F,c)=H₂(F,ℤ)/Q_c.
items.note: API: quotient, universal property for killing these commutators, functoriality preserving c, and finite abelian structure. Tests c=∅ and F cyclic. This definition is independent of a Schur cover.

items.name: Reduced Schur cover
items.statement: Given a Schur cover C→F, quotient C by Q_c in its central kernel to obtain F̃_c→F, with kernel H₂(F,c).
items.note: API: exact central sequence, induced quotient maps and lifting of commuting c-pairs. This extension can depend on the chosen Schur cover; no canonical cover is asserted.

items.name: Conjugacy classes lift bijectively in a reduced cover
items.statement: For x∈c, every conjugacy class of F̃_c lying over the class of x maps bijectively onto that class.
items.note: If two conjugating lifts have the same downstairs effect, their quotient lies over a centralizer element; the defining reduced relation kills the commutator.

items.name: Root-of-unity correction subgroup
items.statement: For a global field K, μ_K denotes its finite group of roots of unity; H₂(F,c)[|μ_K|] is the kernel of multiplication by |μ_K|, written multiplicatively as h^{|μ_K|}=1. For ℚ its cardinality is the 2-torsion cardinality, and for Fq(t) the (q−1)-torsion cardinality.
items.note: API: torsion-kernel subgroup, finiteness and cardinality under isomorphism. Tests μ_ℚ={±1} and μ_Fq(t)=Fqˣ; never replace this by all of H₂.

items.name: Nonabelian imaginary moment conjecture
items.statement: For a finite G and good admissible G′≤G≀C2, Conjecture 1.1 predicts E⁻(G,G′)=|H₂(G′,c)[2]|/|Aut_G′(G)| over ℚ.
items.note: This is a proposition being conjectured, not a theorem. API: rigid equivalent Ẽ⁻=|H₂[2]| and specialization to odd abelian G.

items.name: Nonabelian real moment conjecture
items.statement: Under the same good-type hypotheses, Conjecture 1.1 predicts E⁺(G,G′)=|H₂(G′,c)[2]|/(|c|·|Aut_G′(G)|).
items.note: Conjectural only. API: rigid equivalent Ẽ⁺=|H₂[2]|; test the extra real factor |c|.

items.name: Bad-type divergence conjecture
items.statement: For admissible G′ which is not good, Conjecture 1.1 predicts E⁻(G,G′)=E⁺(G,G′)=+∞.
items.note: Conjectural in general; §7 proves the elementary 2-group family. No all-group divergence theorem is attributed to Wood.

items.name: Odd-order types have no 2-torsion correction
items.statement: If |G| is odd and G′ is admissible, G′ is good and |H₂(G′,c)[2]|=1.
items.note: Goodness follows by conjugacy of the order-two Sylow subgroups. The reduced-multiplier 2-primary vanishing input still needs its complete supplier proof extracted; retained in the handoff.

items.name: Abelian admissible type
items.statement: For abelian finite G, the only admissible embedded type is the generalized dihedral subgroup generated by (a,a⁻¹,1) and swap. For odd |G| it is good; for even |G| it is not good.
items.note: State the actual inversion embedding and prove generation/projection; no implication that every abelian even group has the same bad growth exponent.

items.name: Global lifting-invariant input
items.statement: Take a finite F with a surjection π:F→C2 whose outside involutions form one conjugacy class c, a global K with char K∤|F|, a continuous tame φ:G_K→F taking inertia into c∪{1}, and a chosen reduced cover F̃_c. Put L=K(μ_{4|F̃_c|}) and choose c0∈c.
items.note: API: restrict to G_L, chosen-cover transport, and char hypotheses. φ need not be surjective. Test the trivial homomorphism. The factor 4 supplies μ4 for Grunwald–Wang.

items.name: Tame lift after cyclotomic base change
items.statement: With /34, φ|G_L admits a continuous lift φ̃:G_L→F̃_c that is tamely ramified.
items.note: Separate existence of a global lift from removing finitely many wild local behaviors. Inputs: central obstruction, local tame lifts, Poitou–Tate, Chebotarev and Grunwald–Wang.

items.name: Finite extension-class splitting criterion
items.statement: For an abstract group G, a commutative coefficient group M with G-action, and normalized factor set α, its associated group extension admits a homomorphic splitting iff its H²(G,M) class is zero.
items.note: Read TauCeti/GroupTheory/GroupExtension/Cohomology.lean:226–248, namespace TauCeti.FactorSet. This is the abstract criterion; continuity and the Galois embedding problem are additional work.

items.name: Global obstruction detected locally in the lifting situation
items.statement: For L and A=H₂(F,c) in /34, the localization H²(G_L,A)→∏_v H²(G_Lv,A) is injective: Poitou–Tate identifies its kernel dual with the locally trivial H¹ of the dual module, which vanishes because L contains the requisite roots of unity and no nontrivial finite extension splits at every place.
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.4 owns the global finite-module duality. Exact Milne I.4.10 specialization, archimedean modification and function-field coefficient range require a source check; this item is not certified by an abstract H² declaration.

items.name: Local tame Galois presentation
items.statement: For a nonarchimedean local field with residue cardinality r, its tame quotient has tame inertia generator τ and Frobenius σ with στσ⁻¹=τ^r, with the appropriate prime-to-residue-characteristic completion and Frobenius convention.
items.note: Import the tame quotient owner. API: finite tame maps from images satisfying this relation and reciprocity normalization; no free profinite presentation with wild inertia discarded.

items.name: Grunwald–Wang adjustment in the μ4 case
items.statement: For a number field L containing μ4 and a finite abelian group A, continuous homomorphisms G_Lv→A specified at finitely many places extend to a global continuous G_L→A homomorphism. Apply this to the discrepancy between a global lift and chosen tame local lifts at primes dividing |F̃_c|.
items.locator: Lemma 3.2 proof, p.11; Artin–Tate Ch.X Thm.5
items.note: The exact Grunwald–Wang source and exceptional-case removal need independent reading. In positive characteristic prime-to-|F̃_c| no wild adjustment is needed. This is a weak homomorphism prescription, not a surjective realization theorem.

items.name: Canonical representative over 1 or c0
items.statement: For f∈F̃_c whose image is in c∪{1}, define z(f) to be the unique conjugate of f whose image is c0 when the image is in c, and f itself when the image is 1.
items.note: API: well-definedness via /27, conjugacy invariance, central-kernel equivariance, z on the kernel; test f=1.

items.name: Local inertia element attached to a root of unity
items.statement: For u∈μ_L and a place v of L, choose γ_v in inertia whose image under local reciprocity in the maximal tame abelian quotient of exponent |F̃_c| is the image of u.
items.note: API: existence, local reciprocity quotient, change of lift and finite support of φ̃(γ_v). The element is chosen only through the finite quotient, not as a canonical inertia element.

items.name: Arithmetic lifting product
items.statement: With /34–/41, I_F,π,K(φ,u)=∏_v z(φ̃(γ_v)), over all places of L; only finitely many factors are nonidentity.
items.note: API: finite support, product order independence, all choice-independence lemmas /43–/49, and I(φ,1)=1. Choice of reduced cover remains part of the data.

items.name: Local lifting factors commute
items.statement: Any two elements of F̃_c mapping into {1,c0} commute; hence the factors in the arithmetic lifting product commute.
items.note: Two lifts of c0 differ by a central kernel element; every lift of 1 is central.

items.name: Independence of chosen local inertia lifts
items.statement: The value z(φ̃(γ_v)) depends only on the prescribed root u in the tame abelian exponent-|F̃_c| quotient, not on the choice of γ_v.
items.note: Use that the relevant local image lies in the commuting preimage of {1,c0}, so factors through the chosen abelian quotient.

items.name: Independence of the global tame lift
items.statement: Replacing φ̃ by any other tame lift of φ|G_L does not change I(φ,u).
items.note: The two lifts differ by a global A-valued character. Its product on the diagonal root-of-unity idele is 1 by global reciprocity.

items.name: The product lies in the reduced multiplier
items.statement: The image of I(φ,u) in F is 1, so I(φ,u)∈H₂(F,c).
items.note: Apply global class field theory to the quadratic quotient and its parity of local contributions; centrality alone does not prove the image is trivial.

items.name: Independence of c0
items.statement: Changing the chosen representative c0 in c does not change I(φ,u), after using the same reduced cover.
items.note: Conjugate the entire product and use that /46 places it in the central kernel.

items.name: Conjugation invariance of the Galois homomorphism
items.statement: Conjugating φ by any element of F leaves I(φ,u) unchanged.
items.note: Lift the conjugating element and combine global-lift independence and centrality.

items.name: Cyclotomic torsion restriction
items.statement: I(φ,u)^{|μ_K|}=1; hence I takes values in H₂(F,c)[|μ_K|].
items.note: The proof compares conjugate places and cyclotomic powers, then computes the common divisor of cyclotomic differences. This is the roots-of-unity correction, not the whole multiplier.

items.name: Power compatibility of the invariant
items.statement: For every integer a and u∈μ_L, I(φ,u^a)=I(φ,u)^a.
items.note: Choose compatible local γ_v powers and use commuting factors. Includes a=0 and −1.

items.name: Hom-valued arithmetic invariant
items.statement: For fixed φ the map u↦I(φ,u) is a homomorphism μ_L→H₂(F,c)[|μ_K|]; its target Hom group has cardinality |H₂(F,c)[|μ_K|]|.
items.note: API: evaluate at a generator, product law using cyclicity of μ_L, and count homomorphisms. Evaluation at an arbitrary nongenerator need not be bijective.

items.name: Local reciprocity functoriality
items.statement: For a finite extension of local fields, the local Artin maps commute with field norm and restriction; on units they identify finite abelian tame quotients with the matching inertia quotients.
items.note: Import normalization and norm compatibility from upstream ClassFieldTheory. API test unramified constant-field extensions and roots of unity.

items.name: Global reciprocity kills diagonal elements
items.statement: The product of local reciprocity images of a diagonal element of a global field is trivial in every finite abelian Galois quotient; apply this to roots of unity.
items.note: Import the global Artin map, its diagonal kernel and norm compatibility; keep place normalization fixed.

items.name: Prime-to-p Tate module and generator torsor
items.statement: Over Fq of characteristic p, let Ẑ^(p′)=lim_(n,p)=1 ℤ/n and Ẑ^(p′)(1)=lim_(n,p)=1 μ_n with the compatible power transition maps. Its generator torsor Ẑ^(p′)(1)× is a torsor under (Ẑ^(p′))×.
items.note: API: evaluation at finite level, Frobenius/cyclotomic action, generator change, and comparison with roots in increasing constant fields via norms. Never include the p-primary Tate factor here.

items.name: Twist of a set with a power action
items.statement: For a set X with an action of (Ẑ^(p′))×, X⟨−1⟩ is the set of equivariant maps from the generator torsor Ẑ^(p′)(1)× to X. Galois acts by precomposition with its action on that torsor.
items.note: API: evaluation bijection after choosing a generator, Frobenius convention and functorial maps. The action on X may fail to be by group automorphisms.

items.name: Prime-to-p punctured-line fundamental group
items.statement: For U=P¹ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p with r finite punctures and ∞ removed, its maximal prime-to-p étale fundamental group has a free prime-to-p presentation on finite peripheral generators δ1,…,δr with δ1⋯δrδ∞=1.
items.note: Qualified form needed by the proof. The printed phrase identifying the entire tame fundamental group with this free pro-prime-to-p group is too broad; finite targets of order prime to p factor through the required quotient.

items.name: Topological lifting product
items.statement: For a tame φ:G_F̄q(t)→F with inertia in c∪{1}, |F| prime to p, selected reduced cover and chosen lifts [g] of c, J(φ)= [φ(δ1)]⋯[φ(δr)], where δi are compatible finite peripheral generators.
items.note: API: image in F is φ(δ∞)⁻¹, prescribed generator convention, and universal component invariant /60. The raw product should not be treated as independent of arbitrary changes in generator choices.

items.name: Multidiscriminant
items.statement: For φ as in /57 and a compatible generator of the Tate torsor, N_φ∈ℤ^(c/F) records the number of finite branch points in each conjugacy class; its Tate-twisted form transforms by the power permutation of classes.
items.note: API: nonnegative coordinates, total finite branch degree, generator change and finite-field descent. Test one class and distinguish the infinity contribution.

items.name: Universal component invariant
items.statement: Combine the product of chosen lifts and N_φ to obtain an element of (F̃_c×_(F^ab)ℤ^(c/F))⟨−1⟩, using the discrete action and the inverse of the boundary monodromy convention.
items.note: API: compatibility in the fiber product, evaluation, inertia at infinity and class counts. This uses the universal marked extension, not a naked reduced multiplier.

items.name: Choice independence and Galois covariance of the component invariant
items.statement: The twisted component invariant of a branched (F,c)-cover is independent of ordered peripheral generators with compatible common Tate image and is Galois equivariant.
items.note: Read EVW12 Proposition 8.5.2 and its full proof on pp.49–50, plus the Galois covariance statement/proof on pp.50–51. The construction is a set-valued twisted invariant; the supporting tangential-basepoint infrastructure has not yet been fully decomposed.

items.name: Arithmetic and topological lifting invariants agree up to the stated factors
items.statement: Let F be finite, q of characteristic p∤|F|, π:F→C2 surjective, and c the single conjugacy class of outside involutions. Let φ:G_Fq(t)→F be continuous and tame, with every inertia image in c∪{1}. Fix a reduced cover, its marking and compatible geometric peripheral generators δ_i as in Definition 3.12. For L=Fq(t)(μ_{4|F̃_c|}), there is u∈μ_L such that J(φ|G_F̄q(t))=[c0]^m I(φ,u)[φ(δ∞)]⁻¹, where m is the number of geometric ramified points including ∞ if ramified, c0∈c, and [1]=1.
items.note: The proof ends with I(φ,u)⁻¹, absorbed by replacing u by u⁻¹ using Lemma 3.11. Its constant-field extension splits the geometric branch points; local norm compatibility and global reciprocity compare the two products. This does not imply independence of the selected reduced cover.

items.name: Marked central extension
items.statement: For finite F and a generating conjugacy-invariant c⊆F, a c-marked central extension is a central surjection E→F with a conjugacy-equivariant section c→E. Morphisms preserve the map and marking.
items.note: API: category, composition, equality on marked generators and universal-object uniqueness. Test the split extension.

items.name: Universal marked central extension
items.statement: For generating c⊆F, define F̃ by generators [g], g∈c, and relations [x][y][x]⁻¹=[xyx⁻¹]. The map [g]↦g is a central surjection, universal among c-marked central extensions.
items.note: API: presentation maps, marking, central kernel, unique marked lift and multidegree homomorphism. Unlike a usual universal central extension this does not require F perfect.

items.name: Fiber-product model of the universal extension
items.statement: For finite F generated by c, choose a reduced Schur cover F̃_c and conjugacy-equivariant lifts of c. Then [g]↦(ĝ,e_[g]) identifies F̃ with F̃_c×_(F^ab)ℤ^(c/F).
items.note: The fiber product uses the class map ℤ^(c/F)→F^ab. This identification depends on the marking; the isomorphism type of the universal extension does not. The proof uses the homological universal-coefficient exact sequence and its five-term comparison, which need their own construction checks.

items.name: Power action on finite groups
items.statement: For a finite group F of order prime to p and α∈(Ẑ^(p′))×, define x^α by exponentiation modulo order(x). This is an action on the underlying set and permutes power-stable conjugacy classes.
items.note: API: independence of exponent representative, composition and conjugacy compatibility. Test a nonabelian F: do not assert power maps are group homomorphisms.

items.name: Central correction for the discrete action
items.statement: For chosen conjugacy-equivariant lifts ĝ_i of representatives g_i∈c_i, set z_i(α)=ĝ_i^(−α)·widehat(g_i^α)∈H₂(F,c), and Z_m(α)=∏_i z_i(α)^{m_i}.
items.note: API: independence of representative within c_i, centrality, additivity in multidegree and finite-product order independence. The chosen marking remains fixed.

items.name: Discrete cyclotomic action
items.statement: On F̃≅F̃_c×_(F^ab)ℤ^(c/F), define α*(h,m)=(h^α Z_m(α),m^α), with m^α the permutation of class coordinates. This gives a (Ẑ^(p′))×-action on the underlying set.
items.note: API: preservation of the fiber product, identity/composition, projection to F and multidegree equivariance, and q versus q⁻¹ fixed-point equivalence. Do not upgrade to group automorphisms.

items.name: Odd-parity fixed-point fiber
items.statement: Let F be finite of even order, generated by a union c=⋃c_i of involution classes, q coprime to |F|, y∈c_k, and m∈ℤ^(c/F) with m_k odd and other coordinates even. Exactly |H₂(F,c)[q−1]| pairs (x,m) over y in F̃ are fixed by q⁻¹*.
items.note: Generation is retained from the universal-extension setup. No positivity of the integer m_i is needed for this algebraic theorem.

items.name: Even-parity fixed-point fiber
items.statement: With the hypotheses of /68, if every m_i is even, the fiber over y=1 and multidegree m has exactly |H₂(F,c)[q−1]| points fixed by q⁻¹*.
items.note: Write a lift as ŷh. The equation is h^(1−q)=ŷ^(q−1)∏ĝ_i^((1−q)m_i); even parity makes the right side a (q−1)st power.

items.name: Nonempty power-map fibers are torsion cosets
items.statement: For a finite abelian group A, the solutions of h^d=a are empty or a coset of A[d], so every nonempty fiber has cardinality |A[d]|. In /68–/69 the parity calculation proves nonemptiness.
items.note: This elementary finite-group adapter should use existing kernel/coset APIs. It does not prove every parity vector is soluble; source Remark 4.2 includes an extra class/lift-square obstruction.

items.name: Marked arithmetic extension
items.statement: For a global Q with chosen place ∞, a marked (F,c)-extension is a finite Galois M/Q with an isomorphism π:Gal(M/Q)≅F, inertia images in c∪{1}, and a Q∞-algebra map M⊗Q Q∞→Q̄∞. Isomorphisms preserve π and the marking.
items.note: API: marked isomorphisms, chosen representative M⊆Q̄, induced infinity homomorphism and automorphism rigidity. The marking is an algebra map even if M⊗Q Q∞ is not a field.

items.name: Infinity type of a marked extension
items.statement: The marking induces Gal(Q̄∞/Q∞)→Gal(M/Q); composition with π is the infinity type.
items.note: API: change of marking by conjugation, trivial type iff complete splitting, tame inertia and Frobenius images.

items.name: Imaginary surjections versus marked extensions
items.statement: For an admissible embedded G′ and a ramified infinity type φ∞ with image generated by the distinguished swap, pairs (K,ρ) of quadratic K with the prescribed local completion and a type-G′ surjection correspond bijectively to marked (G′,c)-extensions of Q with infinity type φ∞.
items.note: Qualified to the admissible setting used by the paper. The printed isolated proposition only says subgroup; the inverse projects ker π onto G, which requires that projection surjective. /142 records the counterexample to the unqualified reading.

items.name: Real twisted surjections versus marked extensions
items.statement: For admissible embedded G′, triples (K,ρ,y) with K/Q quadratic split at ∞ and (ρ,y) of type G′ correspond bijectively to marked (G′,c)-extensions with trivial infinity type.
items.note: The reverse construction uses the distinguished swap in G′. Retain admissibility rather than silently adding a twist to a subgroup that has no swap.

items.name: Discriminant in the marked-extension correspondence
items.statement: For either bijection /73–/74, Disc(M/Q)=Disc(K/Q)^{|G′|/2}.
items.note: Use the discriminant tower and that M/K is unramified. For function fields include infinity consistently; for absolute number-field norms use the absolute-value convention.

items.name: Configuration scheme
items.statement: Over ℤ[1/|F|], Conf_n is the open subset of affine n-space parametrizing monic degree-n polynomials with nonzero discriminant, equivalently n distinct unordered points of A¹. It is smooth of relative dimension n.
items.note: API: universal punctured line, ordered cover PConf_n, S_n action, and Fq points ↔ squarefree monic polynomials. n∈ℕ, not an arbitrary integer.

items.name: Marked Hurwitz scheme
items.statement: For finite centerless F generated by involution classes c, the marked Hurwitz scheme CHur_F,n over ℤ[1/|F|] is finite étale over Conf_n; hence smooth of relative dimension n.
items.note: API: moduli functor, tangent marking at infinity, finite étale branch map and characteristic restriction. Centerlessness is retained; this extraction does not assert the stack construction is a scheme for general F.

items.name: Restricted Hurwitz locus
items.statement: For q coprime to |F|, g∈c∪{1}, and a nonnegative class-count vector m with sum n, CHur_F,m^{c,g} is the open-and-closed locus with finite branch multidegree m, prescribed tame inertia g at ∞ and specified Frobenius lift acting trivially there.
items.note: API: openness/closedness, base change, disjoint multidegree strata and the exact infinity type. Negative class counts are excluded even though the theorem prints m∈ℤ^(c/F).

items.name: Hurwitz rational points classify marked extensions
items.statement: CHur_F,m^{c,g}(Fq) is in bijection with marked (F,c)-extensions of Fq(t) of finite branch multidegree m and the prescribed infinity type: tame inertia generator maps to g and the fixed Frobenius lift maps to 1.
items.note: Both directions and automorphism/marking normalization are needed; a coarse moduli set without marking would change the moment weights.

items.name: Stable geometric components and lifting invariants
items.statement: For F as in /77, there is N0 depending only on F such that, when every m_i≥N0, Frobenius-fixed geometric components of CHur_F,m^{c,g} are in bijection with q⁻¹-discrete-action-fixed twisted invariants of multidegree m projecting to g.
items.note: The condition is on every coordinate, not only their sum. Since g is 1 or an involution, the inverse-boundary convention causes no sign change. Wood explicitly says the withdrawn EVW sections do not affect this input; do not claim a full audit of that fact.

items.name: Component label matches the extension invariant
items.statement: Under /79–/80, the label of the geometric component containing a rational point equals the component invariant of the associated marked extension.
items.note: Compatibility of two constructions is a separate theorem, needed to count one fixed invariant.

items.name: Compactly supported Poincaré duality
items.statement: For a smooth separated finite-type n-dimensional scheme X over an algebraically closed field, ℓ invertible, rational ℓ-adic cohomology has a perfect pairing H_c^i(X,Qℓ)×H^{2n−i}(X,Qℓ(n))→Qℓ; in particular their dimensions agree.
items.note: Import the existing duality owner and its Frobenius normalization; no second duality construction inside arithmetic statistics.

items.name: Weight bound for compact cohomology
items.statement: For a separated finite-type X/Fq, every eigenvalue of geometric Frobenius on H_c^j(X̄,Qℓ) for constant coefficients has every complex absolute value at most q^{j/2}.
items.note: Constant sheaf is pure of weight zero; use the Rf_! upper-weight bound. This upper bound does not assert purity of ordinary cohomology for a nonproper variety.

items.name: Trace formula for rational point counts
items.statement: For separated finite-type X/Fq and ℓ∤q, #X(Fq)=∑_j(−1)^j Tr(Frob_geom|H_c^j(X̄,Qℓ)).
items.note: Generic supplier ownership and the pinned TraceFormula roadmap stage need a fresh exact match; leave unrouted in this checkpoint rather than assign the formula to a weight-theory stage.

items.name: Ordered configuration compactification
items.statement: PConf_n admits a smooth proper compactification with relative normal-crossing boundary in the setting used by EVW16 Lemma 7.6; the ordered pullback of the Hurwitz cover is the comparison object.
items.note: API: boundary strata, finite tame cover, reduction and ordered-to-unordered S_n descent. Exact EVW16 source proof and coefficient assumptions remain to be checked.

items.name: Uniform Betti comparison for the Hurwitz family
items.statement: For fixed F,c,g and n, the Betti numbers of CHur_F,m^{c,g} over F̄q, with sum m_i=n, are bounded independently of q coprime to |F| by the corresponding characteristic-zero Betti data.
items.note: Use ordered configuration, EVW16 Proposition 7.7, extension from Z/ℓ to Z/ℓ^a, inverse limit/Qℓ and S_n invariants, taking ℓ>n and ℓ∤q. The required nonproper comparison is stronger than the smooth proper WC.4 contract; do not mark it already supplied by that layer.

items.name: Top-degree trace on one component
items.statement: For a geometrically connected smooth n-dimensional component C defined over Fq, H_c^{2n}(C̄,Qℓ)≅Qℓ(−n), and geometric Frobenius has trace q^n.
items.note: Use duality with H⁰=Qℓ and the Tate twist. A Frobenius-fixed geometric component descends because it is open and closed in this smooth family.

items.name: Uniform component point estimate
items.statement: For F,c as in /77 and g∈c∪{1}, each positive integer n has a constant K_n such that for all q coprime to |F|, all nonnegative m with sum n and every Frobenius-fixed geometric component C of CHur_F,m^{c,g}, |#C(Fq)−q^n|≤K_n q^{n−1/2}.
items.note: Fixed F,c are suppressed in K_n. This is uniform in q for fixed n, with no bound uniform as n→∞. No homological stability theorem is used.

items.name: Monic squarefree polynomial count
items.statement: Over Fq, there are q^d−q^{d−1} monic squarefree polynomials of degree d≥2; degree 1 has q and degree 0 has one.
items.note: The d≥2 boundary matters; prove by the polynomial zeta/Möbius identity or equivalent recurrence, using existing polynomial and finite-field carriers.

items.name: Imaginary exact slice parametrization
items.statement: For odd q, quadratic extensions with infinity completion Fq(√t)∞ and discriminant norm q^{2n} correspond to monic squarefree polynomials of degree 2n−1, via y²=f(t).
items.note: The leading square class is fixed by the prescribed local completion. For n≥2 the denominator is q^{2n−1}−q^{2n−2}. The infinity contribution is one.

items.name: Real exact slice parametrization
items.statement: For odd q, quadratic extensions split at infinity and of discriminant norm q^{2n} correspond to monic squarefree polynomials of degree 2n. Thus the denominator is q^{2n}−q^{2n−1} for n≥1.
items.note: Splitting at infinity fixes the leading square class. Infinity contributes zero to the discriminant degree; the repeated +1 in one proof sentence is incompatible with this case.

items.name: Imaginary per-component unit moment
items.statement: Fix finite G and centerless good admissible G′. For n sufficiently large, and for each q coprime to |G′| any Frobenius-fixed component invariant f_q of multidegree 2n−1 over the swap, the average over IQ_=q^{2n} of type-G′ surjections with invariant f_q tends to 1 as q→∞.
items.note: n is fixed before q tends to infinity; f_q may vary with q. It is a rigid average and has no Aut or |c| denominator.

items.name: Real per-component unit moment
items.statement: Fix finite G and centerless good admissible G′. For fixed sufficiently large n and every choice of Frobenius-fixed f_q of multidegree 2n over 1, the average over RQ_=q^{2n} of type-G′ pairs (ρ,y) with invariant f_q tends to 1 as q→∞ through prime powers coprime to |G′|.
items.note: This is the real rigid pair count; dividing by |c|·|Aut_G′(G)| is a later conversion.

items.name: Imaginary normalized function-field moment
items.statement: For a finite G and centerless good admissible G′, for each sufficiently large fixed n, lim_(q→∞,(q,|G′|)=1) E⁻_Fq(t),=q^{2n}(G,G′)/|H₂(G′,c)[q−1]|=1/|Aut_G′(G)|.
items.note: The torsion cardinality can vary with q; it is divided out inside the limit. This is not the fixed-q large-discriminant Cohen–Lenstra assertion.

items.name: Real normalized function-field moment
items.note: Apply the real per-component estimate and the exact rigidification multiplicity.

items.name: Many large parity vectors
items.statement: For N≥2 and fixed N0, the number of integer N-tuples with every entry ≥N0, prescribed parity in each coordinate, and sum 2n−ε is bounded below by a positive constant times n^{N−1} for all sufficiently large n whenever the parity of the sum is compatible.
items.note: Reduce to compositions after subtracting the least admissible entry and dividing by 2. The constant depends on N,N0, not q.

items.name: Bad-type lower bound established by the component argument
items.statement: For centerless admissible bad G′ and sufficiently large fixed n, the normalized rigid imaginary and real exact-slice averages have liminf_(q→∞,(q,|G′|)=1) at least a positive constant depending only on G,G′ times n^{N_G′−1}.
items.note: Use the explicit parity fibers of Proposition 4.1, /96 and nonnegative contributions from other components. This is the lower-bound conclusion; the printed limit existence is separately flagged in /143.

items.name: Restriction to tame quadratic extensions
items.statement: IQ_X^{tame} and RQ_X^{tame} restrict the quadratic families used in §5 to tame ramification, in particular no ramification at 2 over ℚ; define Ẽ⁻_{≤X,h} by requiring the arithmetic lifting value I(φ,u)=h, and Ẽ⁺_{≤X,h} by the analogous pair count.
items.note: API: local-2 condition, refined counts, disjoint fibers and recovery by summing h. Requires a specified u; no independence from nongenerator choices is asserted.

items.name: Refined conjecture as printed
items.statement: Conjecture 5.1 takes good G′, a root u∈μ_{Q(μ_{4|G̃′_c|})} and h∈H₂(G′,c)[|μ_Q|], and predicts each refined tame rigid moment is 1.
items.note: Unresolved as printed: u=1 makes I(φ,u)=1 for every φ, so a nonidentity h has zero count. A generator/full-Hom formulation may be intended, but is not silently substituted. No route until the precise corrected target is chosen; /144 records the obstruction.

items.name: Malle–Bhargava local model
items.statement: For a fixed finite G′ and the allowed inertia conditions, form D(s)=∏_p[(1/|G′|)∑_(φ:G_Qp→G′ allowed) Disc(πφ)^(−s)], where π:G′→C2 and the discriminant is of its quadratic quotient.
items.note: API: finite local mass, groupoid/isomorphism weight comparison, unramified term and Euler coefficients. This is a model for global counting, not an asserted global Euler product identity.

items.name: Good-prime local factor
items.statement: For p odd with p∤|G′|, the normalized local factor in /100 is 1+N_G′p^(−s), where N_G′ is the number of outside-involution conjugacy classes.
items.note: Use the tame relation and orbit-stabilizer. At ramified primes the inertia element is an involution and commuting Frobenius choices give one mass per class. Retain the exceptional local factors.

items.name: Quadratic field count
items.statement: For quadratic number fields of either fixed real or imaginary signature, the number with absolute discriminant at most X is X/(2ζ(2))+o(X).
items.note: Count fundamental discriminants, including the 2-adic congruence classes. No random model enters this denominator.

items.name: Predicted logarithmic growth
items.statement: Question 6.1 asks whether for every admissible pair (G,G′) there are positive constants c⁺,c⁻ such that E_X^±(G,G′)/(c^±(log X)^{N_G′−1})→1 as X→∞.
items.note: Question only in general; distinguish it from the function-field lower bound and the proven elementary-2-group family.

items.name: Abelianization of a good type
items.statement: For good admissible G′, its abelianization is C2 via the wreath projection.
items.note: It is generated by the image of one conjugacy class of involutions, and the quotient to C2 is surjective. Generation is supplied by admissibility.

items.name: Cyclotomic intermediate-field restriction
items.statement: For a good G′-extension M/ℚ counted here, every abelian intermediate extension of ℚ lies in its quadratic subfield K. Consequently every nontrivial cyclotomic intermediate field equals K, and a fixed K contributes only finitely many counted extensions.
items.note: Use /104 and bounded-degree unramified extension finiteness. This rules out the particular fixed cyclotomic subfield mechanism discussed there; it does not prove the Malle–Bhargava prediction.

items.name: Elementary two-group embedded type
items.statement: For k≥1 take G=C2^k and G′=C2^{k+1} embedded as (a,a,b) in (G×G)⋊C2. Its kernel is the diagonal C2^k and c consists of all 2^k elements with last coordinate nontrivial, so N_G′=2^k.
items.note: API: subgroup/embedding, admissibility, distinct singleton conjugacy classes and coordinate projection. Test k=1; the type is bad.

items.name: Idelic local-character parametrization over ℚ
items.statement: Restriction identifies continuous homomorphisms from the idele class group of ℚ to C2^{k+1} with continuous homomorphisms from ∏_p ℤ_pˣ to that finite group; global reciprocity determines the infinity character by the product of φ_p(−1).
items.note: Import global class-field correspondence and the standard idele-class decomposition over ℚ; its explicit adapter to the product of local units remains a named construction. Surjectivity is imposed separately.

items.name: Allowed elementary-two local characters
items.statement: A local φ_p:ℤ_pˣ→C2^{k+1} is allowed iff its image intersects C2^k×{1} trivially, equivalently it is trivial or generated by an involution with nontrivial last coordinate.
items.note: API: finite enumeration, restriction to −1, induced quadratic character/discriminant and local weight; the prime 2 requires its full unit square-class quotient.

items.name: Archimedean selector
items.statement: For an allowed global elementary-two character, ∏_pφ_p(−1)=1 gives complete real splitting; the imaginary family occurs when this product has nontrivial last coordinate. Other products violate the unramified-over-K infinity condition.
items.note: This is the global reciprocity sign constraint; it couples local factors and prevents using their product without a selector.

items.name: Character-projected Dirichlet series
items.statement: For k≥1 set F_k(s)=2^(−k−1)∑_(χ:C2^{k+1}→{±1})∏_p∑_(φ_p allowed)χ(φ_p(−1))Disc(πφ_p)^(−s). Its coefficients count allowed global homomorphisms with trivial infinity image, before imposing surjectivity.
items.note: API: finite character sum, orthogonality selector, Euler coefficients and convergence for Re s>1. Include the trivial global homomorphism.

items.name: Odd-prime local factors for the real selector
items.statement: For p odd, the local factor of /110 equals 1+2^k p^(−s) if χ=1 or p≡1 mod 4; if p≡3 mod 4 and ker χ=C2^k×1 it is 1−2^k p^(−s); for other nontrivial χ at p≡3 mod 4 it is 1.
items.note: The last case cancels 2^(k−1) positive and negative weights. This statement deliberately excludes p=2.

items.name: Leading singularity of the elementary-two series
items.statement: F_k is analytic for Re s>1 and has leading pole order 2^k at s=1 with positive leading coefficient; the resulting coefficient partial sums satisfy ∑_{n≤X}[n^(−s)]F_k(s)∼c_k X(log X)^(2^k−1) for some c_k>0.
items.note: This combines a singularity assertion and its application; the next pass must split the exact analytic continuation/error hypotheses, local 2-factor positivity and Tauberian theorem. A pole at one point alone is insufficient. Status remains partial.

items.name: Nonsurjective homomorphisms have lower growth
items.statement: For fixed k≥1, allowed nonsurjective homomorphisms counted by F_k are bounded by a k-dependent constant times the corresponding lower-rank counts, plus the trivial homomorphism, and are o(X(log X)^(2^k−1)).
items.note: Classify proper subgroups compatible with the quadratic quotient and use the smaller logarithmic exponent. Treat k=1 boundary separately; source uses F_(k−1).

items.name: Real elementary-two divergence with growth
items.statement: For G=C2^k, diagonal G′=C2^{k+1}, k≥1, the cumulative real rigid numerator is asymptotic to c′_k X(log X)^(2^k−1), with c′_k>0. Therefore Ẽ⁺=E⁺=+∞.
items.note: Divide by the linear quadratic-field denominator and finite rigidification factor; equality here means both limits are +∞, not equality of the finite averages.

items.name: Imaginary elementary-two divergence with growth
items.statement: For the same pair, the cumulative imaginary rigid numerator is asymptotic to c″_k X(log X)^(2^k−1), with c″_k>0. Therefore Ẽ⁻=E⁻=+∞.
items.note: The article says the imaginary argument is similar; a proof blueprint must supply its nontrivial-last-coordinate character selector and positivity rather than cite the real proof unchanged.

items.name: Finite catalogue of admissible types
items.statement: Section 8.1 lists the admissible abstract types and their outside-involution class counts for every group G of orders 2–15 and for A5 and PSL(3,2); within this range the listed invariant does not depend on which Aut(G)-orbit of embeddings realizes the abstract type.
items.note: API: enumeration of embedded subgroups, diagonal Aut(G)-orbits, abstract-type comparison, and certified class counts. Individual row claims are appended below. GAP output is evidence reported by the paper, not a Lean proof or a reproduction performed here.

items.name: Finite catalogue of good types and reduced multipliers
items.statement: Section 8.2 lists the good admissible abstract types for groups G of orders 2–31 and for A5 and PSL(3,2), giving their reduced multipliers and center sizes; the paper reports no embedding-dependent variation of these invariants in that range.
items.note: API: compare with /116, filter goodness, compute reduced quotient from commuting lifts and certify center. Rows with center size >1 do not satisfy Theorem 1.2. D_n means order n throughout these tables.

items.name: The order-96 A4 type
items.statement: For G=A4 with abelianization a:A4→C3, put H={(g1,g2):a(g1)+a(g2)=0}≤A4×A4 and G′=H⋊C2 where C2 swaps factors. Then |H|=48 and |G′|=96; this is the type used in Appendix A, SmallGroup(96,227).
items.note: API: kernel of the abelianization sum, swap stability, subgroup inclusion into A4≀C2 and projection to A4. Unit test its order and distinguished swap.

items.name: Goodness and center of the appendix type
items.statement: For the embedded order-96 type /118, the outside involutions form one conjugacy class and the center is trivial.
items.note: An independent finite permutation calculation is recorded in the report. The multiplier C2 is a separate source-reported computation; do not claim this follows from the center calculation.

items.name: Reduced multiplier in the appendix type
items.statement: For /118, H₂(G′,c)≅C2. Thus the conjectured imaginary rigid moment is 2.
items.note: Source-reported GAP result, not independently recomputed. A verified Schur cover, all commuting-pair relations and the quotient calculation are required before implementation. The conjectural moment is not a numerical theorem.

items.name: Cubic-field parametrization of cyclic cubic class fields
items.statement: Nowhere-totally-ramified non-Galois cubic fields M3/ℚ correspond, by taking S3 Galois closure M, to unramified cyclic cubic extensions M/K of quadratic fields, with Disc(M3)=Disc(K); retain the imaginary signature for the appendix enumeration.
items.note: API: inverse from the cubic subfields, isomorphism multiplicity, inertia restrictions, and the discriminant identity. Class-field and cubic-field enumeration suppliers must be matched separately.

items.name: Class-group quotients for the A4 search
items.statement: For the sextic S3 field M over its imaginary quadratic K, enumerate subgroups N≤Cl(M) with quotient C2², invariant under Gal(M/K)=C3 but not under Gal(M/ℚ)=S3. Class field theory produces unramified L/M with L/K Galois and L/ℚ non-Galois.
items.note: API: induced Galois action on Cl(M), invariant-kernel tests and field recovery. All subgroups of Cl(M) are normal because Cl(M) is abelian. Tests distinguish C3-stable from S3-stable.

items.name: Schur–Zassenhaus complement
items.statement: For a normal subgroup N of a group G with Nat.card N coprime to its index, there exists a complement H≤G. In the appendix this splits an extension of C3 by C2².
items.note: Read Mathlib/GroupTheory/SchurZassenhaus.lean:274–298. This gives existence, not an automatically canonical complement or an unqualified conjugacy theorem.

items.name: The two C3 actions on C2²
items.statement: Up to the appropriate conjugacy, a C3-action on C2² is trivial or faithful; the faithful semidirect product is A4 and the trivial one is C2²×C3.
items.note: Aut(C2²)≅S3 gives the two classes. The preprint writes C3×C3×C2 in the trivial case, which has order 18 rather than 12; /145 records the correction.

items.name: The selected quotient gives A4
items.statement: For /122, Gal(L/K)≅A4: Schur–Zassenhaus gives C2²⋊C3, and a trivial action would give an abelian extension of K invariant under the quadratic involution by class field theory, contradicting that L/ℚ is not Galois.
items.note: The inverse construction and normal-closure type must be checked. The printed wrong-order trivial group is not used as an input.

items.name: Exact cubic-field enumeration algorithm
items.statement: Use complete cubic-field tables with −X<Disc(M3)<0, retain nowhere-totally-ramified fields (including the separate prime-2 test), compute each S3 closure M, then its class group and the invariant C2² quotients of /122.
items.note: API: input range convention, soundness/completeness of filtering and quotient enumeration, arithmetic precision certificates and conversion from field counts to rigid counts. The paper’s description leaves the explicit Aut(A4) weighting to be audited; /146 keeps that gap open.

items.name: Sampled large-discriminant estimator
items.statement: For larger X=2^k, the appendix samples 1% uniformly with replacement from cubic fields in successive discriminant blocks of width 2^20, applies the same class-group computation, and rescales the sample sum to estimate the rigid A4 moment.
items.note: API: sample space, with-replacement multiplicities, unbiased finite-population estimator and variance; exact table values and sampled estimates must remain separately tagged. This is empirical evidence, not a limit proof.

items.name: Numerical evidence and its range
items.statement: Appendix A reports exact A4 computations through X=2^23 and sampled estimates reaching X=2^32, where the estimate is about 1.26 against the conjectural limit 2. Figure 1 displays exact and sampled curves separately.
items.note: Record a finite data product with method/range tags. The figure does not prove convergence, monotonicity or an error bound; a formal test must never assert that 1.26 equals the predicted limit.

items.name: Hermite finiteness
items.statement: For a fixed extension Ω/ℚ and a bound B, there are finitely many number fields inside Ω with absolute field discriminant at most B.
items.note: Read Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Discriminant/Basic.lean:494–510 at 082e2d3. The finite set is of intermediate fields F/ℚ in a fixed extension with FiniteDimensional ℚ F and |discr F|≤N. This does not itself prove the relative-field or function-field finiteness adapters.

items.name: Class fields and equivariance
items.statement: Finite abelian extensions of a global K unramified at finite places and split at infinity correspond to finite quotients of the ordinary ideal class group, equivariantly for automorphisms of K.
items.note: Upstream owns the class-field correspondence and Hilbert class field. The equivariance and normal-closure adapters used by the appendix need exact interfaces.

items.name: Universal coefficients for central extensions
items.statement: For a group F and trivial coefficient module A, the universal-coefficient exact sequence 0→Ext¹(H₁(F,ℤ),A)→H²(F,A)→Hom(H₂(F,ℤ),A)→0 relates a central extension to its homological class map.
items.note: Build on the existing group homology/cohomology and extension classification. A complete pinned declaration search for this exact natural sequence, transgression compatibility and signs remains required; no scalar-Schur-multiplier shortcut.

items.name: Reduced-cover homology image
items.statement: For a reduced Schur cover f:F̃_c→F, the image H₂(F̃_c,ℤ)→H₂(F,ℤ) equals Q_c, the kernel of H₂(F,ℤ)→H₂(F,c).
items.locator: EVW12 Definition 7.3 and following paragraph, p.34
items.note: Required for the fiber-product universal property. Use the homological five-term exact sequence and the extension-class comparison; those are not supplied merely by a carrier definition.

items.name: Marked fiber-product abelianization
items.statement: For F generated by c, and P=ℤ^(c/F)×_(F^ab)F̃_c with its chosen lifted marking ĉ, the map ℤ^(ĉ/P)→P^ab is an isomorphism.
items.note: Keep the generating hypothesis from the surrounding theorem. The proof’s last elementary group calculation is left to the reader and must be supplied in the design.

items.name: Stable braid-orbit classification
items.statement: For finite F generated by c, the universal lifting invariant bijects connected Hurwitz braid orbits of sufficiently large multidegree m with the fiber of F̃ over m; sufficiently large means every class multiplicity ≥A(F,c).
items.note: This stable π0 theorem is the input, not a higher homology stability theorem. Its proof needs the eventual bijectivity of stabilization on generating tuples, not merely a surjection.

items.name: Specialization preserves component invariants
items.statement: For compatible marked covers over a strictly henselian trait with group order invertible, specialization identifies the relevant prime-to-residue-characteristic peripheral fundamental groups and preserves the twisted lifting invariant, after restricting Tate modules to prime-to-p factors.
items.note: Exact SGA1 tame-specialization and tangential-basepoint compatibility supply the claim. Do not compare unrestricted geometric fundamental groups across mixed characteristic.

items.name: Tangential marking at infinity
items.statement: Choose a uniformizer at ∞ and compatible prime-to-characteristic roots. The associated tangential fiber functor gives the marked cover and a specified inertia map at infinity, compatible with tame base change.
items.note: API: fiber functor, marking after adjoining an Nth root, Abhyankar-lemma étaleness, and Frobenius lift. Full §8.2 source decomposition remains open, not replaced by a chosen rational point in an unramified fiber.

items.name: Imaginary odd-order known moment cases
items.statement: The introduction cites the imaginary C3 moment Ẽ⁻(C3,S3)=1 from Davenport–Heilbronn and several nonabelian low-degree cases from Bhargava and Alberts.
items.note: Only the explicit C3 formula is transcribed here; the other cited cases and their rigid/unrigid conventions need separate items after reading the original statements. This inventory is partial for that reason; no blanket theorem about all known moments is exported.

items.name: Analytic Euler-product to counting interface
items.statement: To pass from the Euler product in §6 or F_k in §7 to a count ∼C X(log X)^(r−1), specify nonnegative coefficients, the right-half-plane convergence, a pole of order r with positive principal coefficient and the exact boundary regularity required by the chosen Tauberian theorem.
items.note: This is an unresolved source/interface item, not a theorem saying a pole alone suffices. Check whether upstream Chebotarev’s Tauberian theorem supplies the needed higher-order form or requires a Part II. Leave unrouted pending that exact audit.

items.name: Prime-two local factor and imaginary selector
items.statement: Complete the §7 Euler-product calculation by enumerating continuous allowed maps ℤ₂ˣ→C2^{k+1}, attaching conductor/discriminant exponents, and using the character projector for infinity image outside C2^k×1 in the imaginary case.
items.note: Finite local character space is explicit but this checkpoint has not transcribed the resulting factor or imaginary projector into separate theorem statements. These are required to justify the stated positive constants and are left unrouted as a concrete gap.

items.name: Safe scope of the function-field conclusion
items.statement: The proved good-type theorem fixes sufficiently large n and sends q to infinity through prime powers coprime to |G′|; it requires centerless G′. It does not establish the fixed-q limit as discriminant grows, or the analogous number-field conjecture.
items.note: A statement/API guard: acceptance examples vary q at fixed n and reject attempts to exchange the two limits without a new uniform estimate.

items.name: Bad-type normalization transfer
items.statement: The rigid bad-type lower bound /97 implies the same positive-constant n^{N_G′−1} liminf lower bound for unrigid E^± divided by |H₂(G′,c)[q−1]|, since the corresponding rigidification multiplicities are fixed finite positive numbers depending on the type.
items.note: For the real bad case use A(G,G′), not the good-only formula |c||Aut_G′(G)|. This transfer does not by itself prove existence of the printed ordinary limit.

items.name: Counterexample to unqualified marked correspondence
items.statement: Take G=C3 and G′ equal to the subgroup generated by the bare swap in G≀C2. There are marked quadratic G′-extensions with a permitted ramified infinity type, but there is no surjection onto C3 of that type because the kernel projection of G′ is trivial.
items.note: Concrete regression test: choose Q=ℚ and K=ℚ(√−3). The right side includes this quadratic marked extension and the left side is empty. This is an extraction-authored check, not a proposition attributed to Wood.

items.name: Bad-type limit-existence gap
items.statement: Theorems 1.2 and 4.8 write an ordinary q-limit for bad types. The displayed proof obtains a lower bound by selecting parity-compatible large-multiplicity components; this immediately yields a liminf bound, but additional control is needed to prove the ordinary limit exists across all allowed q.
items.note: Not a claim the limit is false. Resolve the q-dependence of all remaining fixed-component fibers, or explicitly distinguish the printed statement from the established lower-bound interface. Unrouted pending exact proof/source resolution.

items.name: Identity-root obstruction to the printed refined conjecture
items.statement: For every admissible lifting input, I(φ,1)=1. Thus if h≠1 the count defined by I(φ,1)=h is zero at every height with a nonempty denominator, and cannot have average limit 1.
items.note: This is a direct algebraic obstruction to arbitrary-u quantification when the correction subgroup is nontrivial. It leaves open which primitive-generator or Hom-valued conjecture should replace the printed one.

items.name: Order check for the appendix trivial action
items.statement: The trivial semidirect product (C2×C2)⋊C3 has order 12 and is C2²×C3. The printed C3×C3×C2 has order 18 and cannot be that extension.
items.note: A source correction certificate verified directly by cardinalities; preserve it in algorithm tests.

items.name: Unresolved rigid weighting of the A4 enumeration
items.statement: An unrigid A4-extension supplies rigid surjections by choosing Gal(L/K)≅A4; its multiplicity must be reconciled with the exact embedded type and the enumeration of kernels of class-group quotients before dividing by the quadratic-field count.
items.note: The prose says the algorithm computes Ẽ⁻, but does not explicitly display the Aut(A4) weighting. Reconstruct the weighting and check sample field/quotient multiplicities before claiming reproducibility. Unrouted pending this check.

routes.brief:
Extend the existing upstream roadmap “Induction, restriction, and Mackey theory for finite groups” after its Layer 7 central extensions/representation groups. The parent is the first prerequisite. Import its Schur-cover existence and factor-set classification, Mathlib groupHomology.H2 on the trivial integral representation, and TauCeti’s existing normalized factor sets and splitting criterion. Do not reconstruct induction, projective representations or ordinary Schur covers. TauCeti.schurMultiplier is H²(F,kˣ), whereas this extension uses H₂(F,ℤ); build and name the universal-coefficient comparison with all natural maps instead of treating these as definitionally equal.

Layer A: commuting-pair classes in integral H₂, their realization as commutators of lifts, independence of lifts, naturality and orientation. Construct Q_c generated by the classes with x∈c,y∈C_F(x), the quotient H₂(F,c), and the quotient of a chosen Schur cover. Prove exactness/centrality, canonical independence of the quotient homology group from the cover, and the bijective lift of each c-conjugacy class. Do not claim a canonical reduced extension. Check cyclic groups, empty c and the two Schur covers D8/Q8 of C2². Audit and construct the necessary universal-coefficient and homological five-term statements once, on the existing group homology/cohomology carriers.

Layer B: c-marked central extensions and the universal presentation on symbols [g], with [x][y][x]⁻¹=[xyx⁻¹]. Prove its universal property, the chosen-marking isomorphism with F̃_c×_(F^ab)ℤ^(c/F), the abelianization lemma and the reduced-cover H₂ image theorem. Read EVW12 v1 §§7.2–7.5 completely, including the elementary calculation left to the reader. The rational/power-stable c requirement is added only for the next layer; generation is required for the central surjection throughout.

Layer C: prime-to-p power actions, the marking correction z_i(α), the discrete action on the set underlying the universal extension, projection/multidegree equivariance and the two parity fixed-point counts in Wood Proposition 4.1. Use integer multidegrees here; only Hurwitz consumers impose nonnegativity. A nonempty power fiber is a torsor under H₂(F,c)[q−1]; prove nonemptiness in the stated parity cases, and keep the general parity obstruction separate. Include a nonabelian test proving why the power/discrete action cannot be declared an action by group automorphisms.

Layer D: certified finite reduced-multiplier examples from Wood §8.2, with explicit embedded groups and full SmallGroup(order,index) identifiers, not only the bracketed index. Start with the order-96 A4 type: its concrete embedding is the kernel of the sum A4²→C3, extended by factor swap. The separate statistics consumer owns its extension counts. Prove the C2 reduced multiplier by an explicit cover and relation certificate before treating the source GAP output as checked. Other table rows remain source-reported until similarly certified. Center computations and type enumeration are consumed from the arithmetic-statistics finite examples, not built twice.

Every definition needs constructor/eliminator, transport/naturality API, equality and representative-independence lemmas, and executable small-group unit tests. Suggested future home: TauCeti/GroupTheory/SchurCover/Reduced. ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 consumes only the finite multiplier/torsion cardinalities; InverseGalois IG.3/IG.5 consumes the universal marked extension and discrete fixed-point fibers; IG.4 supplies the arithmetic lifting product using global duality and reciprocity. These consumers must not feed back into the foundational supplier. Read the exact EVW inputs despite the 2013 withdrawal notice: Wood states that the affected §§6,12 are not used, but this is not a certificate for a stronger stability theorem. This checkpoint leaves explicit source and ownership gaps outside this route; a design must not silently absorb the unrouted Tauberian, trace-formula or conjecture-correction items.
routes.reason: Upstream Layer 7 owns ordinary Schur covers and factor sets, but not reduced multipliers, commuting-pair quotients, universal marked central extensions or the discrete component action. This is its natural continuation; the arithmetic and geometric consumers import it. The integral homology carrier is already in Mathlib and is not rebuilt.
